review_notes: I read the whole file and the Coloring definitions it uses. I grepped the Mathlib tree for uses of the sum-coloring declarations (`Coloring.sum`, `sumLeft`, `sumRight`, `sumEquiv`) and found none outside this file. I found no simp loops or competing rules. `sum_adj_inl`, `sum_adj_inr` and `not_adj_sum_inl_inr` are all proved by plain `simp` via the `@[simps!]` lemma `sum_adj`, so adding simp attributes to them would be redundant. The one gap I'm confident about is the missing evaluation lemmas for the coloring constructors. I did not run Lean, so the proposed `@[simps]` or explicit lemmas are untested. In particular I haven't checked how `simps` handles the `Coloring` abbreviation.

findings.excerpt:
def Coloring.sum (cG : G.Coloring γ) (cH : H.Coloring γ) : (G ⊕g H).Coloring γ where
  toFun := Sum.elim cG cH
findings.problem: The coloring constructors and destructors have no simp lemmas that evaluate them. Only the round-trip identities `sumLeft_sum`, `sumRight_sum` and `sum_sumLeft_sumRight` are tagged `@[simp]`. Because `Coloring.sum`, `sumLeft` and `sumRight` are irreducible-to-simp defs, `simp` cannot reduce `(cG.sum cH) (Sum.inl v)` to `cG v`, or `c.sumLeft v` to `c (Sum.inl v)`. The only way to compute with them is `rfl`, as the file does itself in `ext (u | u) <;> rfl` and the `rfl` proofs of `sumLeft_sum` and `sumRight_sum`. `Coloring.sumEquiv` also has no `apply`/`symm_apply` simp lemmas, so `Coloring.sumEquiv c` and `Coloring.sumEquiv.symm p` stay opaque to `simp`. Other defs in this file, such as `Hom.sum`, `Embedding.sum` and `Iso.sumCongr`, do get `@[simps]` evaluation lemmas, so the coloring section is inconsistent with them.
findings.proposed_change: Add evaluation lemmas as simp lemmas. Either put `@[simps]` on `Coloring.sum`, or state them explicitly: `@[simp] lemma Coloring.sum_apply_inl (cG) (cH) (v : V) : cG.sum cH (.inl v) = cG v := rfl`, the analogous `sum_apply_inr`, and `@[simp] lemma Coloring.sumLeft_apply (c : (G ⊕g H).Coloring γ) (v : V) : c.sumLeft v = c (.inl v) := rfl`, with the matching `sumRight_apply`. Add `@[simps]` (or explicit `sumEquiv_apply` / `sumEquiv_symm_apply` lemmas) to `Coloring.sumEquiv`.
findings.benefit: Users and later proofs get a canonical normal form: values of a sum coloring reduce to values of the component colorings, and `sumLeft`/`sumRight` unfold to plain evaluation on `inl`/`inr`. They can then use `simp` instead of `rfl` or manual unfolding, as `sum_sumLeft_sumRight` and `sumEquiv.left_inv` currently do. The new rules are terminating and do not conflict with the existing round-trip rules.
